title: Mac Monitor telemetry 1.3.0
description: The records Mac Monitor writes: its JSONL and pretty exports, and the macmonitor command line's output. Each record is eslogger's JSON for an Endpoint Security event plus Mac Monitor's enrichments; every key is marked x-mac-monitor-origin: eslogger or mac-monitor, and everything under a Mac Monitor key is Mac Monitor's. One kind of line is not an event's record: a process snapshot, which has a process_snapshot key and follows #/$defs/process_snapshot_record. A network flow's record, whose event key is new_flow or flow_closed, is Mac Monitor's own: it follows #/$defs/network_record, and its process is a flow_process. Each GitHub release attaches the schema as Mac-Monitor.telemetry.schema.json, and the latest is at https://github.com/Brandon7CC/mac-monitor/releases/latest/download/Mac-Monitor.telemetry.schema.json.

boot_session_uuid.description: Which start of the Mac the event is from: the kernel's boot session UUID (`sysctl kern.bootsessionuuid`), new at every start. A pid and a pid version, and so a process key in `ancestor_keys`, mean one process only within a boot session, so join records on `sensor_id`, `boot_session_uuid` and the key. null in a trace that didn't record it, such as eslogger's.

context.description: A summary of the event, as Mac Monitor's event list shows it.

global_seq_num.description: The message's sequence number among all, for the client that received it: Mac Monitor's numbers never match eslogger's.

indicators.description: The indicators in this Mac's saved set (Settings > Indicators, `macmonitor indicators`) that this event matched, evaluated by the Security Extension as it captured the event (`evaluated_by: security_extension`). When the Security Extension did not evaluate the event, these are the indicators Mac Monitor matched as it wrote the record (`evaluated_by: export`). Empty when none matched. The indicators the Security Extension could not rule out are in `indicators_undetermined`. Absent when nothing was evaluated: the writer had no indicators to match, or the record is from Mac Monitor before 3.1.0.

indicators_undetermined.description: The indicators in this Mac's saved set that the Security Extension could not rule out for this event, in the set's order, at most 32. `reason` says why: `scan_budget` when evaluating the event's values exceeded the Security Extension's per-event scan budget, and `value_limit` when a value that isn't ASCII was longer than the 64 KiB the Security Extension compares. Each may or may not match. While `indicators` has fewer than 32 entries and `indicators_undetermined` fewer than 32, an indicator in neither did not match. A list at its limit may have been cut short, and then an indicator in neither may match. A consumer that must not miss a match should treat both lists as possible matches; one that wants only certain matches reads `indicators`. Absent when every indicator was decided, or the record wasn't evaluated by the Security Extension (`evaluated_by: export` never writes it).

macOS.description: The macOS version of the Mac that recorded the event: 27.0 (Build 26A1).

sensor_id.description: The Sensor ID of the Mac Monitor that recorded the event.

seq_num.description: The message's sequence number among its type's, for the client that received it: Mac Monitor's numbers never match eslogger's.

sip_status.description: System Integrity Protection on the Mac that recorded the event, as csrutil status names it: enabled, disabled, or custom when only some protections are off. null in a trace that didn't record it, such as eslogger's.

target_path.description: The path the event is about, or "Not supported".

telemetry_version.description: The version of Mac Monitor's telemetry schema the record follows.

result.description: Absent when `result_type` is neither ES_RESULT_TYPE_AUTH nor ES_RESULT_TYPE_FLAGS.

auth_human.description: The name of `auth`: ES_AUTH_RESULT_ALLOW or ES_AUTH_RESULT_DENY.

result_type_human.description: The name of `result_type`. Absent when `result_type` is neither ES_RESULT_TYPE_AUTH nor ES_RESULT_TYPE_FLAGS.

data.description: The arm `type` names. Empty for a type Mac Monitor doesn't know.

auto_unlock.description: An Apple Watch unlocked the Mac or approved an authorization prompt: es_event_authentication_auto_unlock_t.

type_string.description: The name of `type`, from the SDK's constants.

od.description: Open Directory checked a record's password: es_event_authentication_od_t.

instigator.description: The process that asked for the authentication: the XPC caller.

record_name.description: The record's name: for Users, the user name.

token.description: CryptoTokenKit authenticated with a token: es_event_authentication_token_t.

instigator.description: The process that asked for the authentication: the XPC caller.

kerberos_principal.description: Given when the token got a ticket-granting ticket.

pubkey_hash.description: The hash of the public key.

touchid.description: Touch ID verified or identified a user: es_event_authentication_touchid_t.

instigator.description: The process that asked for the authentication: the XPC caller.

touchid_mode_string.description: The name of `touchid_mode`, from the SDK's constants.

uid.description: The user authenticated, for a verification that succeeded. Unsigned.

uid_human.description: The name of `uid`: null without one, or for a user this Mac doesn't know.

type_string.description: The name of `type`, from the SDK's constants.

id.description: Mac Monitor's identifier for the result.

rule_class_string.description: The name of `rule_class`, from the SDK's constants.

authorization_petition_event.description: A process asked for authorization rights: es_event_authorization_petition_t.

flags_array.description: The names of the flags `flags` has.

file_type.description: What `target` is by its content, never its name: the Launch Services type identifier of its first 4 KB, sniffed by the Mac that recorded the event when it recorded it, only when `modified` is true (an unmodified close's file isn't read). A Mach-O is com.apple.mach-o-executable, -dylib, -bundle, -object or -core by its filetype, else com.apple.mach-o-binary (a universal binary by the slice the recording Mac runs, else its first; one whose slice is a static library is public.archive). A script is named by its #! interpreter, through /usr/bin/env too: public.zsh-script, public.python-script, com.apple.applescript.text for osascript (com.netscape.javascript-source with -l JavaScript), else public.script. Compiled AppleScript and JXA (FasdUAS, JsOsaDAS) are com.apple.applescript.script, and Java class files com.sun.java-class. Archives (an Apple Archive raw or compressed, as aa archive writes it), disk images (a UDIF trailer), ELF and PE binaries, property lists and PDFs have their own; other UTF-8 text without a NUL is public.plain-text, and anything else public.data. Or `empty` for a file of 0 bytes by the event's stat, `dyld_shared_cache` for a dyld shared cache (its first bytes are dyld_v1), and `replaced` when the path no longer names `target`: its device or inode differ, or a symbolic link is on the path now. null when the file isn't read: not a regular file, dataless, on a volume that isn't local, gone, a path Endpoint Security cut short, or not readable by the process's effective user and group. Also null when the event wasn't recorded by Mac Monitor 3.1.0 or later (an eslogger trace, or one exported before 3.1.0): the file is read only at capture, never when a trace is opened. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

mach_o_type.description: The mach-o/loader.h name of a Mach-O's filetype, read with `file_type`: MH_EXECUTE, MH_DYLIB, MH_BUNDLE, MH_OBJECT, MH_CORE, MH_DYLINKER, MH_KEXT_BUNDLE, MH_FILESET, MH_DSYM and the others, or its value in hex (0x1f) for one without a name. A universal binary's is that of the slice `file_type` names it by. null when `target` isn't Mach-O, or as `file_type` is. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

yara_scan.description: What scanning the written file with Apple's XProtect rules found, on the Mac that recorded the event, when it recorded it. A modified close carries it while scanning is on, for a Mach-O executable, library, bundle, kernel extension or dynamic linker, a #! script, a shell script or AppleScript by its extension, or compiled AppleScript or JXA, by `file_type` and `mach_o_type`. Since telemetry 1.3.0. Absent when the file isn't one that's scanned, scanning was off, or the event wasn't recorded by Mac Monitor 3.3.0 or later.

destination.description: The destination: an existing file, or a new path, as `destination_type` says.

existing_file.description: Absent when the destination is a new path.

new_path.description: A file not yet created: its directory, name and mode.

is_quarantined.description: Whether the file was quarantined when the event was recorded: 1 if it had a com.apple.quarantine attribute, 0 if not, 2 if it wasn't found.

cs_invalidated_event.description: A process's code signature invalidated: es_event_cs_invalidated_t, which has no fields.

event.description: The event: one key, named for its type, as eslogger names it.

ancestor_keys.description: The target's ancestors, nearest first, as they were when its process was forked: each one's pid and pid version, as `pid.pidversion`, which name the exec whose target has that audit token. At most 8: the nearest, and the first below launchd, which is never listed. Empty for a child of launchd, and null when the Security Extension wasn't tracking lineage. Since telemetry 1.2.0.

certificate_chain.description: The target's signing certificates, leaf first. Absent when the target has none.

thumbprint.description: The certificate's SHA-1 fingerprint, in hex.

dyld_exec_path.description: null before message version 7. Absent when the Mac that wrote the record ran macOS 13.0 to 13.2.

executable_age_ms.description: Milliseconds from the target's executable's birth (its stat's st_birthtimespec) to the exec. null when the birth time is unknown.

launched_by_parent.description: The process that really caused the target to run; null when it isn't known.

resolved_script_path.description: The script run: `script`'s path, or, when Endpoint Security reports none, the script an interpreter's arguments name, if the exec's user could read it.

script_content.description: The script's text, read when the event was recorded: only if the exec's user could read it and, for `script`, only while it's still the file Endpoint Security reported. It stops at the first NUL byte and at 1 MiB, and invalid UTF-8 reads as U+FFFD.

where_froms.description: Where the program the exec runs was downloaded from: the strings of the binary property list array in the com.apple.metadata:kMDItemWhereFroms attribute, the download URL and then the page it was found on. They're the first found of the script the exec runs, the bundle the script is the main executable of, the target's executable, and the bundle that is the main executable of. A script is read only if the exec's user could read it. An executable in /System, /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin or /usr/libexec isn't read. Read on the Mac that recorded the event, when it recorded it. Since telemetry 1.3.0. Absent when none of them has the attribute, or the event wasn't recorded by Mac Monitor 3.3.0 or later.

yara_scan.description: What scanning the script the exec runs with Apple's XProtect rules found, on the Mac that recorded the event, when it recorded it. An exec carries it while scanning is on, for `script`, for the script an interpreter's arguments name (`resolved_script_path`), and for the Contents/Resources/Scripts/main.scpt of an AppleScript or JXA applet whose executable in Contents/MacOS it runs, whatever its name. It describes that script, not the exec's target. XPScripts.yr applies to a script osascript runs and to an applet's. Since telemetry 1.3.0. Absent when the exec runs no script Mac Monitor found, scanning was off, or the event wasn't recorded by Mac Monitor 3.3.0 or later.

flow_closed_event.description: A network flow that closed, with the kernel's byte totals.

bytes_inbound_count.description: The bytes the socket received in its life, as the kernel counts them. A flow open before the capture counts from before it. Absent when the kernel's final counts were lost.

bytes_outbound_count.description: The bytes the socket sent in its life. Absent when the kernel's final counts were lost.

direction.description: Which side opened the flow, as the kernel says from macOS 14. Absent when the kernel doesn't say, as on macOS 13 and for most UDP.

first_party_site.description: The site the request was made for, as the process gave it. What the process asked for, from its own network parameters, not observed DNS. Absent when the process named none.

identifier.description: The flow's identifier: the same in its new_flow and its flow_closed while one capture reads the kernel's socket. Reading it again, after every stream and Mac Monitor stopped recording flows, makes new identifiers for flows open across it.

local_endpoint.description: The local address and port. Absent when the kernel gives none.

remote_address_scope.description: Where the remote address is in the address space, from IANA's special-purpose address registries: public, private (RFC 1918 and IPv6 unique local), shared (100.64.0.0/10, for carrier-grade NAT), link_local, loopback, multicast, or reserved (documentation, benchmarking and other addresses never routed across the internet, and IPv6 outside 2000::/3). An IPv4-mapped address, or one in NAT64's well-known prefix 64:ff9b::/96, has its IPv4 address's scope.

remote_endpoint.description: The remote address and port. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address is written as IPv4.

remote_hostname.description: The name of the host the flow is to, with no trailing dot. For a Network.framework or NSURLSession connection, it's the host the process asked for. For a BSD socket, as curl and Python use, it's the name the process set on the socket, or else the name mDNSResponder last resolved the remote address to for the same program, which can come from an earlier run of it. Absent when the process named none, and mDNSResponder resolved no name to the address for it.

socket_type.description: The socket's type: 1 (SOCK_STREAM) for TCP, 2 (SOCK_DGRAM) for UDP and QUIC.

source_app.description: The app a delegated socket acts for, such as the app that asked mDNSResponder for a lookup. Absent when the socket isn't delegated.

url.description: A Network.framework connection's URL as the process gave it, nothing redacted. With Record URL paths off it ends at the host and port. At most 2048 bytes. What the process asked for, from its own network parameters, not observed DNS. Absent when the flow isn't a Network.framework TCP or QUIC connection that named one.

address.description: The address, as inet_ntop writes it, with no scope.

flow_process.description: A network flow's process: some of a process's keys, under the same names. A key the socket and Mac Monitor's lineage didn't give is left out, never made up.

audit_token.description: The process's audit token. Absent when neither a read of the running process nor Mac Monitor's lineage gave it.

audit_token_string.description: `audit_token` as one line of text. Absent when neither a read of the running process nor Mac Monitor's lineage gave it.

codesigning_type.description: How the executable is signed. Absent when its signature wasn't read.

euid.description: The effective user ID, from `audit_token`. Absent when neither a read of the running process nor Mac Monitor's lineage gave it.

euid_human.description: The name of the effective user. Absent when there's no `audit_token`, or the user has no name on the Mac that wrote the record.

executable.description: The process's executable. Absent when neither a read of the running process nor Mac Monitor's lineage gave it.

group_id.description: The process group. Absent when the process was gone before its socket was first reported.

pid.description: The process ID: 0 for the kernel.

ppid.description: The parent's process ID. Absent when the process was gone before its socket was first reported.

session_id.description: The session. Absent when the process wasn't running when its socket was first reported.

signing_id.description: The process's signing ID. Absent when the code is unsigned, or its signature wasn't read.

team_id.description: The process's team ID. Absent when the code has none, or its signature wasn't read.

ancestor_keys.description: The child's ancestors, nearest first, the forking process's first: each one's pid and pid version, as `pid.pidversion`. At most 8: the nearest, and the first below launchd, which is never listed. null when the Security Extension wasn't tracking lineage. Since telemetry 1.2.0.

launched_by_parent.description: The process that really caused the child to run; null when it isn't known.

file.description: The file's path, or the file, as `file_type` says; null when the path is NULL. Absent when `file_type` names neither.

file_path.description: The file's path, when `file_type` names a path. Absent when `file_type` doesn't name a path.

file_type_string.description: The name of `file_type`, from the SDK's constants.

sha256.description: The file's SHA-256 in uppercase hex, given for a file under 100 MB. Mac Monitor writes NULL when there's none, where eslogger writes null.

type_string.description: The name of `type`, from the SDK's constants.

indicator.description: An indicator from this Mac's saved set that the event matched.

default.description: Whether it is one of Mac Monitor's default indicators, which Mac Monitor ships. edited says whether this Mac changed it.

edited.description: Whether this Mac changed one Mac Monitor ships: its name, description, symbol, color, predicate, tactic, technique or severity. Always false when default is false.

evaluated_by.description: Who matched it: security_extension, the Security Extension as it captured the event, or export, Mac Monitor as it wrote the record of an event the Security Extension did not evaluate.

id.description: The indicator's identity, the same on every Mac for one Mac Monitor ships.

matched.description: What made it match: the comparisons of its rule the event passed, at most 16. For a sequence, those of its steps this event matched, as it completed it. Only comparisons that say what the event has are listed, not a != a value outside ANY, or anything under NOT. ANY lists the first string of the array that matched, with != too since telemetry 1.3.0. null when none of its comparisons is one of those, and when evaluated_by is export. Since telemetry 1.2.0.

items.description: One comparison of an indicator's rule that the event passed.

field.description: The key path the comparison read, as the rule names it, such as event.exec.target.executable.path, lineage.paths for one of the process's ancestors, or event.close.yara_scan.rules.@count for an array's size since telemetry 1.3.0.

value.description: The value the event had there: for ANY, the one of the array's strings that matched, and for .@count, the array's size. A string's first 256 characters. A whole number past 2^53 is rounded.

name.description: What Settings > Indicators calls it, such as Background item added.

pack.description: The indicator pack this Mac had when the indicator matched, by its sequence, for one Mac Monitor ships. With id and revision it says which rule fired. null for one this Mac added, and when Mac Monitor's indicators are its build's own rather than a pack's. Since telemetry 1.2.0.

revision.description: The indicator's revision, which its indicator pack raises whenever the indicator changes, or null for one without. An edited one keeps the revision it was edited from. Since telemetry 1.2.0.

severity.description: How closely a match is worth looking at: high for behavior that is rare in ordinary use, medium for less common behavior that has ordinary uses, low for context and common behavior. It never changes what matches.

tactic.description: The MITRE ATT&CK tactic it's for, by name, or null for none. Stealth and Defense Impairment since telemetry 1.2.0, when ATT&CK v19 split Defense Evasion into them: Defense Evasion is only in records written before.

tactic_id.description: The tactic's ATT&CK identity, such as TA0003, or null for none. TA0005 is Stealth since telemetry 1.2.0, and Defense Evasion before. TA0112, Defense Impairment, since 1.2.0.

technique.description: The ATT&CK technique it finds, such as T1543.001, or null for none.

indicator_undetermined.description: An indicator from this Mac's saved set that the Security Extension could not rule out for the event: it may or may not match.

default.description: Whether it is one of Mac Monitor's default indicators, which Mac Monitor ships. edited says whether this Mac changed it.

edited.description: Whether this Mac changed one Mac Monitor ships: its name, description, symbol, color, predicate, tactic, technique or severity. Always false when default is false.

evaluated_by.description: Who matched it: security_extension, the Security Extension as it captured the event, or export, Mac Monitor as it wrote the record of an event the Security Extension did not evaluate.

id.description: The indicator's identity, the same on every Mac for one Mac Monitor ships.

matched.description: Always null: an indicator that wasn't decided matched nothing. Since telemetry 1.2.0.

name.description: What Settings > Indicators calls it, such as Background item added.

pack.description: The indicator pack this Mac had when the indicator matched, by its sequence, for one Mac Monitor ships. With id and revision it says which rule fired. null for one this Mac added, and when Mac Monitor's indicators are its build's own rather than a pack's. Since telemetry 1.2.0.

reason.description: Why it wasn't decided: scan_budget when evaluating the event's values exceeded the Security Extension's per-event scan budget, or value_limit when a value that isn't ASCII was longer than the 64 KiB the Security Extension compares.

revision.description: The indicator's revision, which its indicator pack raises whenever the indicator changes, or null for one without. An edited one keeps the revision it was edited from. Since telemetry 1.2.0.

severity.description: How closely a match is worth looking at: high for behavior that is rare in ordinary use, medium for less common behavior that has ordinary uses, low for context and common behavior. It never changes what matches.

tactic.description: The MITRE ATT&CK tactic it's for, by name, or null for none. Stealth and Defense Impairment since telemetry 1.2.0, when ATT&CK v19 split Defense Evasion into them: Defense Evasion is only in records written before.

tactic_id.description: The tactic's ATT&CK identity, such as TA0003, or null for none. TA0005 is Stealth since telemetry 1.2.0, and Defense Evasion before. TA0112, Defense Impairment, since 1.2.0.

technique.description: The ATT&CK technique it finds, such as T1543.001, or null for none.

driver_bundle_id.description: The bundle ID of the service's driver, read from the IOKit registry with `parent_class`: the service's CFBundleIdentifier property, from the personality it matched (a kext's, or a DriverKit extension's own), else that of the nearest provider that has one, the driver that published it: com.apple.iokit.IOSurface. When that names an Apple bundle, or none, and a third-party kext defines the service's class (IOObjectCopyBundleIdentifierForClass), it's that kext, so a kext can't pass as Apple by setting the property. null as `parent_class` is, and when neither source names one. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

parent_class.description: The class of the service being opened, read from the IOKit registry of the Mac that recorded the event, when it recorded it (IOObjectGetClass): IOSurfaceRoot. The service is found by `parent_path` when the entry it finds has the `parent_registry_id`, else by `parent_registry_id`, as siblings can share a path. null before message version 10 (macOS 26), when the service is no longer in the registry, and when the event wasn't recorded by Mac Monitor 3.1.0 or later (an eslogger trace, or one exported before 3.1.0, opened and exported again): the registry is read only at capture, never when a trace is opened. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

parent_path.description: null when Endpoint Security gives none, or in a record from Mac Monitor before 3.0.0, which left out an empty one. Absent when the message's version is before 10 (macOS 26).

parent_registry_id.description: Unsigned. null in a record from Mac Monitor before 3.0.0, which left it out with an empty `parent_path`. Absent when the message's version is before 10 (macOS 26).

app_bundle.description: The bundle at `app_path`, the app a helper, agent or daemon belongs to, of any item type. null when the item has no app, its app isn't a bundle, or, on a remove, it's already gone. Also null when the event wasn't recorded by Mac Monitor 3.1.0 or later (an eslogger trace, or one exported before 3.1.0, opened and exported again): bundles are read only at capture, never when a trace is opened. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

bundle.description: The bundle the item names, for an ES_BTM_ITEM_TYPE_APP, ES_BTM_ITEM_TYPE_LOGIN_ITEM or ES_BTM_ITEM_TYPE_USER_ITEM item whose path (absolute, or relative to `app_path`) is a bundle directory. null for other items, for a path that isn't a bundle, and on a remove when the bundle is already gone. Also null when the event wasn't recorded by Mac Monitor 3.1.0 or later (an eslogger trace, or one exported before 3.1.0, opened and exported again): bundles are read only at capture, never when a trace is opened. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

item_type_string.description: The name of `item_type`, from the SDK's constants.

plist_contents.description: The item's property list as text, read from the Mac that recorded the event, when it recorded it: an agent's or daemon's launchd plist, or the Info.plist of the bundle an app, login item or user item names (`bundle`). A property list stored in binary is converted to XML. Cut at 1 MiB. Not read through a symbolic link below the item's folder, app or bundle. Absent when the item has no property list, or it couldn't be read.

uid_human.description: The name of `uid`, when it's a system account.

launch_item_bundle.description: An app or helper bundle a launch item names, read by the Security Extension from the Mac that recorded the event, when it recorded it: never when a trace is opened. Each value is null when the bundle doesn't have it or it couldn't be read. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

age_ms.description: How old the bundle was at the event: milliseconds from `birth_time` to the message's time, rounded. Negative when the clock stepped back between the two. null when `birth_time` is unknown.

birth_time.description: When the bundle directory was created: its st_birthtimespec.

codesigning_type.description: How the bundle as a whole is signed: PLATFORM when its signature has a platform identifier, ADHOC or UNSIGNED, otherwise APP_STORE or DEVELOPER_ID by its certificates (UNKNOWN for others). null when the signature couldn't be read: also when the Info.plist couldn't be, or a FIFO or other special file is where Security would open it.

executable_path.description: The bundle's executable, as CFBundle finds it: Contents/MacOS/ and CFBundleExecutable, or CFBundleExecutable beside a shallow bundle's Info.plist, named whether or not the file exists. NSExecutable without CFBundleExecutable, and without either, the file named as the bundle without its extension, when there's one.

info_plist_path.description: The bundle's Info.plist: Contents/Info.plist, or Info.plist at the top of a shallow bundle. Named whether or not it could be read (it isn't through a symbolic link below the bundle); null only in a record that doesn't name it.

is_background_only.description: LSBackgroundOnly, from the Info.plist, read as `is_ui_element` is: the app runs with no user interface at all.

is_quarantined.description: 1 if the bundle directory has a com.apple.quarantine attribute, 0 if not, and 2 if it couldn't be found.

is_ui_element.description: LSUIElement, from the Info.plist, as a Boolean (also when it's written as a number or as "1", "YES" or "true"): the app runs as an agent, without a Dock icon or menu bar.

name.description: CFBundleDisplayName, else CFBundleName, from the Info.plist.

signing_id.description: The bundle's signing identifier, from a static read of its signature (SecStaticCodeCreateWithPath and SecCodeCopySigningInformation, without validating it). null for an unsigned bundle.

team_id.description: The bundle's team identifier, from its signature. null for Apple platform, adhoc and unsigned bundles.

where_froms.description: Where the bundle was downloaded from: the strings of the binary property list array in the bundle directory's com.apple.metadata:kMDItemWhereFroms attribute, the download URL and then the page it was found on. null without the attribute.

launched_by_parent.description: The process that really caused another to run, and how Mac Monitor knows.

audit_token.description: The launched-by parent's audit token, as eslogger writes one; null when only its pid is known.

launchd_job.description: The launchd job that started the process, for a direct launchd child with a label.

anyOf.description: The launchd job that started the process.

label.description: The job's label, from XPC_SERVICE_NAME in its exec environment.

path.description: The launched-by parent's executable, when known.

resolved_by.description: Who resolved it: the Security Extension, the app, or the opening of a trace.

listextattr_event.description: A file's extended attributes listed: es_event_listextattr_t.

mmap_event.description: A file mapped into memory: es_event_mmap_t.

file_type.description: What `source` is by its content, never its name: the Launch Services type identifier of its first 4 KB, sniffed by the Mac that recorded the event when it recorded it. A Mach-O is com.apple.mach-o-executable, -dylib, -bundle, -object or -core by its filetype, else com.apple.mach-o-binary (a universal binary by the slice the recording Mac runs, else its first; one whose slice is a static library is public.archive). A script is named by its #! interpreter, through /usr/bin/env too: public.zsh-script, public.python-script, com.apple.applescript.text for osascript (com.netscape.javascript-source with -l JavaScript), else public.script. Compiled AppleScript and JXA (FasdUAS, JsOsaDAS) are com.apple.applescript.script, and Java class files com.sun.java-class. Archives (an Apple Archive raw or compressed, as aa archive writes it), disk images (a UDIF trailer), ELF and PE binaries, property lists and PDFs have their own; other UTF-8 text without a NUL is public.plain-text, and anything else public.data. Or `empty` for a file of 0 bytes by the event's stat, `dyld_shared_cache` for a dyld shared cache (its first bytes are dyld_v1), and `replaced` when the path no longer names `source`: its device or inode differ, or a symbolic link is on the path now. null when the file isn't read: not a regular file, dataless, on a volume that isn't local, gone, a path Endpoint Security cut short, or not readable by the process's effective user and group. Also null when the event wasn't recorded by Mac Monitor 3.1.0 or later (an eslogger trace, or one exported before 3.1.0): the file is read only at capture, never when a trace is opened. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

flag_names.description: The names of the bits `flags` has, from sys/mman.h, in bit order, one name per bit: MAP_SHARED, MAP_PRIVATE (not MAP_COPY), MAP_FIXED, MAP_RENAME, MAP_NORESERVE, MAP_RESERVED0080, MAP_NOEXTEND, MAP_HASSEMAPHORE, MAP_NOCACHE, MAP_JIT, MAP_ANON (not MAP_ANONYMOUS), MAP_RESILIENT_CODESIGN, MAP_RESILIENT_MEDIA, MAP_32BIT, MAP_TRANSLATED_ALLOW_EXECUTE, MAP_UNIX03, MAP_TPRO. Empty for flags of 0: MAP_FILE is 0, so it's never named. Bits sys/mman.h doesn't name are left out; `flags` keeps them.

mach_o_type.description: The mach-o/loader.h name of a Mach-O's filetype, read with `file_type`: MH_EXECUTE, MH_DYLIB, MH_BUNDLE, MH_OBJECT, MH_CORE, MH_DYLINKER, MH_KEXT_BUNDLE, MH_FILESET, MH_DSYM and the others, or its value in hex (0x1f) for one without a name. A universal binary's is that of the slice `file_type` names it by. null when `source` isn't Mach-O, or as `file_type` is. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

max_protection_names.description: The names of the bits `max_protection` has, from sys/mman.h, in bit order: PROT_READ, PROT_WRITE, PROT_EXEC. It's a vm_prot_t, named with PROT_* too: its low three bits are VM_PROT_READ, VM_PROT_WRITE and VM_PROT_EXECUTE, the same bits. PROT_NONE alone for 0. Other bits are left out; `max_protection` keeps them.

protection_names.description: The names of the bits `protection` has, from sys/mman.h, in bit order: PROT_READ, PROT_WRITE, PROT_EXEC. PROT_NONE alone for 0. Other bits are left out; `protection` keeps them.

disposition.description: The es_mount_disposition_t: ES_MOUNT_DISPOSITION_UNKNOWN before message version 8.

disposition_string.description: The name of `disposition`, from the SDK's constants.

mprotect_event.description: A memory region's protection changed: es_event_mprotect_t.

flags.description: The names of the flags `protection` has, from mach/vm_prot.h, in bit order: VM_PROT_READ, VM_PROT_WRITE, VM_PROT_EXECUTE. VM_PROT_NONE alone for 0. Other bits are left out; `protection` keeps them.

network_record.description: A network flow's record, Mac Monitor's own: a record whose event key is new_flow or flow_closed follows this definition, not the schema's root. It has no version, schema_version, sequence numbers, thread, action, event_type or es_event_type, which mean Endpoint Security.

boot_session_uuid.description: Which start of the Mac the event is from: the kernel's boot session UUID (`sysctl kern.bootsessionuuid`), new at every start. A pid and a pid version, and so a process key in `ancestor_keys`, mean one process only within a boot session, so join records on `sensor_id`, `boot_session_uuid` and the key. null in a trace that didn't record it, such as eslogger's.

context.description: A summary of the flow, as Mac Monitor's event list shows it: the URL, else the host and port, and for flow_closed the bytes in.

event.description: The flow, under its event's key.

indicators.description: The indicators in this Mac's saved set (Settings > Indicators, `macmonitor indicators`) that this event matched, evaluated by the Security Extension as it captured the event (`evaluated_by: security_extension`). When the Security Extension did not evaluate the event, these are the indicators Mac Monitor matched as it wrote the record (`evaluated_by: export`). Empty when none matched. The indicators the Security Extension could not rule out are in `indicators_undetermined`. Absent when nothing was evaluated: the writer had no indicators to match, or the record is from Mac Monitor before 3.1.0.

indicators_undetermined.description: The indicators in this Mac's saved set that the Security Extension could not rule out for this event, in the set's order, at most 32. `reason` says why: `scan_budget` when evaluating the event's values exceeded the Security Extension's per-event scan budget, and `value_limit` when a value that isn't ASCII was longer than the 64 KiB the Security Extension compares. Each may or may not match. While `indicators` has fewer than 32 entries and `indicators_undetermined` fewer than 32, an indicator in neither did not match. A list at its limit may have been cut short, and then an indicator in neither may match. A consumer that must not miss a match should treat both lists as possible matches; one that wants only certain matches reads `indicators`. Absent when every indicator was decided, or the record wasn't evaluated by the Security Extension (`evaluated_by: export` never writes it).

macOS.description: The macOS version of the Mac that recorded the event: 27.0 (Build 26A1).

mach_time.description: The same time on Endpoint Security's clock (mach_absolute_time), so flows sort with Endpoint Security's events.

sensor_id.description: The Sensor ID of the Mac Monitor that recorded the event.

sip_status.description: System Integrity Protection on the Mac that recorded the event, as csrutil status names it: enabled, disabled, or custom when only some protections are off. null in a trace that didn't record it, such as eslogger's.

telemetry_version.description: The version of Mac Monitor's telemetry schema the record follows.

time.description: When the flow was seen to connect, for new_flow, or to close, as eslogger writes a time: the kernel's time for the report it came from.

new_flow_event.description: A network flow that opened, as the kernel's network statistics socket reported it.

direction.description: Which side opened the flow, as the kernel says from macOS 14. Absent when the kernel doesn't say, as on macOS 13 and for most UDP.

first_party_site.description: The site the request was made for, as the process gave it. What the process asked for, from its own network parameters, not observed DNS. Absent when the process named none.

identifier.description: The flow's identifier: the same in its new_flow and its flow_closed while one capture reads the kernel's socket. Reading it again, after every stream and Mac Monitor stopped recording flows, makes new identifiers for flows open across it.

local_endpoint.description: The local address and port. Absent when the kernel gives none.

remote_address_scope.description: Where the remote address is in the address space, from IANA's special-purpose address registries: public, private (RFC 1918 and IPv6 unique local), shared (100.64.0.0/10, for carrier-grade NAT), link_local, loopback, multicast, or reserved (documentation, benchmarking and other addresses never routed across the internet, and IPv6 outside 2000::/3). An IPv4-mapped address, or one in NAT64's well-known prefix 64:ff9b::/96, has its IPv4 address's scope.

remote_endpoint.description: The remote address and port. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address is written as IPv4.

remote_hostname.description: The name of the host the flow is to, with no trailing dot. For a Network.framework or NSURLSession connection, it's the host the process asked for. For a BSD socket, as curl and Python use, it's the name the process set on the socket, or else the name mDNSResponder last resolved the remote address to for the same program, which can come from an earlier run of it. Absent when the process named none, and mDNSResponder resolved no name to the address for it.

socket_type.description: The socket's type: 1 (SOCK_STREAM) for TCP, 2 (SOCK_DGRAM) for UDP and QUIC.

source_app.description: The app a delegated socket acts for, such as the app that asked mDNSResponder for a lookup. Absent when the socket isn't delegated.

url.description: A Network.framework connection's URL as the process gave it, nothing redacted. With Record URL paths off it ends at the host and port. At most 2048 bytes. What the process asked for, from its own network parameters, not observed DNS. Absent when the flow isn't a Network.framework TCP or QUIC connection that named one.

od_attribute_value_add_event.description: A value added to a record's attribute: es_event_od_attribute_value_add_t.

member.description: null in a record from Mac Monitor before 3.0.0 whose member's type it didn't know.

od_group_remove_event.description: A member removed from a group: es_event_od_group_remove_t.

member.description: null in a record from Mac Monitor before 3.0.0 whose member's type it didn't know.

member_string.description: The name of the member's type.

member_type.description: A user's name (0), a user's UUID (1) or a group's UUID (2).

member_value.description: The user's name, or the UUID; null in a record from Mac Monitor before 3.0.0.

result_type_string.description: The name of `result_type`, from the SDK's constants.

source_address_type_string.description: The name of `source_address_type`, from the SDK's constants.
The name of `source_address_type`, from the SDK's constants.

type_string.description: The name of `type`, from the SDK's constants.

proc_suspend_resume_event.description: A process suspended or resumed: es_event_proc_suspend_resume_t.

type_string.description: The name of `type`, from the SDK's constants.

process.description: A process: es_process_t, as eslogger writes it, with Mac Monitor's enrichments.

codesigning_flag_names.description: The names of the flags `codesigning_flags` sets, from cs_blobs.h, in bit order: CS_VALID, CS_RUNTIME (the hardened runtime), CS_LINKER_SIGNED.

codesigning_type.description: How the executable is signed: from `codesigning_flags`, or its certificates.

cs_validation_category.description: Absent when the message's version is before 10 (macOS 26).

cs_validation_category_string.description: The name of `cs_validation_category`. Absent when `cs_validation_category` is.

euid_human.description: The name of the effective user. Absent when the user has no name on the Mac that wrote the record, or isn't a system account in a trace opened from another Mac.

file_quarantine_type.description: Whether File Quarantine applies to the executable: opted in, forced by Apple, or disabled.

id.description: Mac Monitor's identifier for the process in this record.

process_age_ms.description: How old the process was at the event: milliseconds from `start_time` to the message's time, rounded. Every process in a record has its own. Negative when the clock stepped back between the two. null when `start_time` is unknown (0). Since telemetry 1.1.0.

ruid_human.description: The name of the real user. Absent when the user has no name on the Mac that wrote the record, or isn't a system account in a trace opened from another Mac.

signing_id.description: null when Endpoint Security gives none, or in a record from Mac Monitor before 3.0.0, which left out an empty one.

process_snapshot.description: A process nothing earlier in the file describes: one that was running before the capture started, or whose exec a filter, a selection or a Clear left out. Its fields are named as a process's are.

ancestor_keys.description: The keys of the process's own ancestors, nearest first, as an exec's `ancestor_keys` are. Empty for a child of launchd.

codesigning_type.description: How the process is signed, as a process's `codesigning_type` says it. Absent when its signature was never read.

command_line.description: The process's command line, up to 1024 characters. Absent when it could not be read, or the snapshot was made from a fork.

executable.description: The process's executable. Absent when the process was gone before it could be read.

key.description: The process's key, as `ancestor_keys` names it: its pid, a dot, and its pid version.

signing_id.description: The process's signing ID. Absent when the code is unsigned, or its signature was never read.

team_id.description: The process's team ID. Absent when the code has none, or its signature was never read.

process_snapshot_record.description: A process snapshot's line, the one kind of line that is not an event's record. A line with a `process_snapshot` key follows this definition, not the schema's root. Mac Monitor writes one before the first record that is from a process, or names it in `ancestor_keys`, when nothing earlier in the file describes that process.

boot_session_uuid.description: Which start of that Mac the snapshot is from, as the records beside it carry. Absent when the records beside it carry none, or the line is from a test fixture.

sensor_id.description: The Sensor ID of the Mac the snapshot is from, as its events carry. Absent when the line is from a test fixture, which has every Sensor ID removed.

install_source_string.description: The name of `install_source`, from the SDK's constants.

remote_thread_create_event.description: A thread created in another process: es_event_remote_thread_create_t.

thread_state_string.description: The name of the thread state's flavor, for the architecture of the Mac that recorded it.

destination.description: The destination: an existing file, or a new path, as `destination_type` says.

existing_file.description: Absent when the destination is a new path.

new_path.description: A path that doesn't exist yet: its directory and name.

file_type.description: What `source` is by its content, never its name: the Launch Services type identifier of its first 4 KB, sniffed by the Mac that recorded the event when it recorded it, where it was renamed to, or from the bytes the modified close that wrote that version of it read, as a file written under one name and renamed into place is. A Mach-O is com.apple.mach-o-executable, -dylib, -bundle, -object or -core by its filetype, else com.apple.mach-o-binary (a universal binary by the slice the recording Mac runs, else its first; one whose slice is a static library is public.archive). A script is named by its #! interpreter, through /usr/bin/env too: public.zsh-script, public.python-script, com.apple.applescript.text for osascript (com.netscape.javascript-source with -l JavaScript), else public.script. Compiled AppleScript and JXA (FasdUAS, JsOsaDAS) are com.apple.applescript.script, and Java class files com.sun.java-class. Archives (an Apple Archive raw or compressed, as aa archive writes it), disk images (a UDIF trailer), ELF and PE binaries, property lists and PDFs have their own; other UTF-8 text without a NUL is public.plain-text, and anything else public.data. Or `empty` for a file of 0 bytes by the event's stat, `dyld_shared_cache` for a dyld shared cache (its first bytes are dyld_v1), and `replaced` when the path no longer names `source`: its device or inode differ, or a symbolic link is on the path now. null when the file isn't read: not a regular file, dataless, on a volume that isn't local, gone, a path Endpoint Security cut short, or not readable by the process's effective user and group. Also null when the event wasn't recorded by Mac Monitor 3.1.0 or later (an eslogger trace, or one exported before 3.1.0): the file is read only at capture, never when a trace is opened. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

is_quarantined.description: Whether the file was quarantined when the event was recorded: 1 if it had a com.apple.quarantine attribute, 0 if not, 2 if it wasn't found.

mach_o_type.description: The mach-o/loader.h name of a Mach-O's filetype, read with `file_type`: MH_EXECUTE, MH_DYLIB, MH_BUNDLE, MH_OBJECT, MH_CORE, MH_DYLINKER, MH_KEXT_BUNDLE, MH_FILESET, MH_DSYM and the others, or its value in hex (0x1f) for one without a name. A universal binary's is that of the slice `file_type` names it by. null when `source` isn't Mach-O, or as `file_type` is. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

yara_scan.description: What scanning the written file with Apple's XProtect rules found, on the Mac that recorded the event, when it recorded it. A rename carries the scan of the modified close that wrote the file it moves, while scanning is on, as a file written under one name and renamed into place is. Nothing is scanned for a rename itself. Since telemetry 1.3.0. Absent when the file isn't one that's scanned, scanning was off, or the event wasn't recorded by Mac Monitor 3.3.0 or later.

mode_added.description: What the change added that's worth a look, in this order: executable (an execute bit, as chmod +x gives), setuid, setgid and world_writable (S_IWOTH). A directory gets none of the first three, and a sticky directory (1777, as /tmp is) not world_writable either. Without `previous_mode`, every bit `mode` sets counts as added. Derived when the record is written. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

mode_symbolic.description: `mode`'s permission bits as `ls -l` shows them, without the file type: rw-r--r--. Setuid and setgid show in the owner's and group's execute place as s, or S without execute, and the sticky bit in others' as t or T. Derived from `mode` when the record is written. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

previous_mode.description: The file's permission bits before the change (st_mode & 07777): Endpoint Security's stat of `target` is from before it. null when `target` has no stat. Derived when the record is written. Since telemetry 1.1.0.

signing_id.description: null when the signing information has none.

team_id.description: null when the signing information has none, as for adhoc signing.

st_ino.description: Unsigned: 2^63 or more on some network file systems.

identity_type_string.description: The name of `identity_type`, from the SDK's constants.

reason_string.description: The name of `reason`, from the SDK's constants.

right_string.description: The name of `right`, from the SDK's constants.

update_type_string.description: The name of `update_type`, from the SDK's constants.

thread.description: The thread that took the action: es_thread_t.

state_base64.description: The state's bytes in base64: null when they weren't kept.

uipc_bind_event.description: A Unix domain socket bound: es_event_uipc_bind_t.

uipc_connect_event.description: A Unix domain socket connected: es_event_uipc_connect_t.

domain_string.description: The name of `domain`, from the SDK's constants.

protocol_string.description: The name of `protocol`, from the SDK's constants.

type_string.description: The name of `type`, from the SDK's constants.

service_domain_type_string.description: The name of `service_domain_type`, from the SDK's constants.

yara_scan.description: What scanning a file with Apple's XProtect rules found: a written file, or the script an exec runs. The rules are the ones the recording Mac's XProtect has, run with the YARA that macOS ships, and a match is what XProtect's rules say of the file. XProtect.yara applies to every file scanned, and XPScripts.yr to AppleScript and JXA, as XProtect itself applies them.

names.description: XProtect's name for each rule in `rules`, in the same order, from the rule's description, such as MACOS.OSASCRIPT.BOZO. A rule without a description is named by its identifier.

report_only.description: The rules in `rules` that XProtect only reports and never acts on (match_type = 4), such as its hunting rules, by identifier.

rules.description: Every rule that matched, by its identifier, such as XProtect_MACOS_OSASCRIPT_BOZO. Empty when none did, or the file wasn't scanned.

status.description: scanned, or why the file wasn't: too_large (over 32 MB), over_budget (the scanner's share of the CPU was spent), busy (the scan couldn't finish within half a second behind the files before it), unreadable (gone, dataless, or not readable by the process that wrote or runs it), changed (written again before it was read, so the close of that write is scanned), unavailable (Apple's rules couldn't be loaded on that Mac), timed_out or too_many_matches (libyara stopped the scan). The next exec of a script that was over_budget or busy asks again.

xprotect_version.description: The XProtect version whose rules scanned it, such as 5377. null when no rules were loaded.
